A minimum-variance portfolio puts its money where the estimated risk is
lowest. This article builds one such strategy from the history tools of
`vignette("causal-history", package = "ledgr")`: it estimates a covariance
matrix from daily returns once a month, solves for the long-only weights with
the smallest estimated variance, and turns them into share targets. Every step
uses ledgr's public functions, so the same strategy runs in a single backtest,
a sweep and on parallel workers.

Three choices that an estimator usually hides are made explicit here: which
instruments enter the estimate, what happens to a holding the estimate leaves
out, and what the strategy does on a day it cannot estimate at all.

The solver comes from the `quadprog` package. The code chunks that run the
strategy are evaluated only when it is installed:

```r
install.packages("quadprog")
```

## The Demo Data

The demo is three years of simulated sessions for eight instruments from
`ledgr_sim_pit_inputs()`, with two changes to its bars, so that the screens
below have something to screen:

- `DEMO_05` trades thinly from June to November 2019: it has no print on
  every second session, so ledgr carries its previous close forward on those
  sessions.
- `DEMO_08` is listed late: its first print is on 3 September 2019.

```{r}
#| label: demo-data
#| message: false

library(ledgr)

ids <- sprintf("DEMO_%02d", 1:8)
pit <- ledgr_sim_pit_inputs(ids, from = "2018-01-01", to = "2020-12-31", seed = 7L)
bars <- pit$bars
day <- as.Date(bars$ts_utc)
thin <- sort(unique(day[day >= as.Date("2019-06-01") & day <= as.Date("2019-11-30")]))
skipped <- thin[seq(2L, length(thin), by = 2L)]
bars <- bars[!(bars$instrument_id == "DEMO_05" & day %in% skipped), ]
day <- as.Date(bars$ts_utc)
bars <- bars[!(bars$instrument_id == "DEMO_08" & day < as.Date("2019-09-03")), ]

facts <- ledgr_facts(
  ledgr_facts_sessions(pit$sessions, venue_id = "DEMO_VENUE",
                       knowledge = "evidenced", timezone = "UTC"),
  ledgr_facts_membership_snapshots(pit$membership, universe_id = "DEMO_UNIVERSE",
                                   complete = TRUE, knowledge = "evidenced"),
  ledgr_facts_trading_status(pit$trading_status, knowledge = "evidenced"),
  ledgr_facts_lifetime(pit$lifetime, knowledge = "evidenced"),
  ledgr_facts_equity_corporate_actions(pit$corporate_actions)
)
snapshot_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "minimum-variance-demo.duckdb")
if (file.exists(snapshot_path)) unlink(snapshot_path)
snapshot <- ledgr_snapshot_from_df(
  bars, instruments_df = pit$instruments, facts = facts,
  db_path = snapshot_path, snapshot_id = "minimum_variance_demo",
  price_basis = "split_adjusted"
)
pit$cases
```

The simulated inputs also hold the teaching cases of
`vignette("point-in-time-inputs", package = "ledgr")`. All of them fall in
the first two weeks of 2018. One of them is a cash dividend on `DEMO_03` on
10 January 2018. The strategy holds nothing until its first decision a year
later, so no dividend is posted in this demo; the run below says so. The bars
are split-adjusted and exclude distributions, so the strategy estimates risk
from price returns.

## The Strategy

The whole strategy is one function. Everything it needs is defined inside it,
because preflight refuses a strategy that calls a helper from the calling
session.

```{r}
#| label: strategy

min_variance <- function(ctx, params) {
  lookback <- params$lookback %||% 252L
  threshold <- params$threshold %||% 0.2
  shrink <- params$shrink %||% 0.5
  min_obs <- params$min_obs %||% 60L
  keep_excluded <- params$keep_excluded %||% TRUE
  hold <- function(outcome) structure(ctx$hold(), outcome = outcome)

  # 1. Decide only on a month's first session: the session whose UTC month
  #    differs from that of the previous expected venue session. The data
  #    start has no previous session and counts as a month start.
  axis <- ctx |>
    ledgr_history_frame(bar = "close", lookback = 2L, instruments = character())
  months <- format(axis$ts_utc, "%Y-%m", tz = "UTC")
  if (length(months) == 2L && months[[1L]] == months[[2L]]) {
    return(hold("not_a_decision_date"))
  }

  # 2. Read closes over the window and screen out instruments whose window
  #    holds too many carried prices.
  closes <- ctx |> ledgr_history_frame(bar = "close", lookback = lookback)
  if (!ledgr_history_sufficient(closes)) {
    return(hold("insufficient_history"))
  }
  selection <- ledgr_history_info(closes)$selection
  selection <- selection[selection$requested, , drop = FALSE]
  candidates <- selection$instrument_id[selection$carried_input_share <= threshold]

  # 3. Read daily returns of the remaining instruments, missing cells kept,
  #    and screen out instruments with too few valid returns. Read again, so
  #    the final read holds exactly the instruments that are estimated.
  returns <- ctx |>
    ledgr_history_frame(feature = "return_1", lookback = lookback,
                        instruments = candidates, na_action = "keep")
  valid <- colSums(is.finite(ledgr_history_matrix(returns)))
  estimated <- ledgr_history_info(returns)$included_ids[valid >= min_obs]
  if (length(estimated) < 2L) {
    return(hold("too_few_instruments"))
  }
  returns <- ctx |>
    ledgr_history_frame(feature = "return_1", lookback = lookback,
                        instruments = estimated, na_action = "keep")

  # 4. Estimate a pairwise covariance and shrink it toward its diagonal.
  sigma <- stats::cov(ledgr_history_matrix(returns), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  sigma <- (1 - shrink) * sigma + shrink * diag(diag(sigma))
  if (anyNA(sigma)) {
    return(hold("covariance_not_positive_definite"))
  }
  eigenvalues <- eigen(sigma, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  if (min(eigenvalues) <= 1e-10 * max(eigenvalues)) {
    return(hold("covariance_not_positive_definite"))
  }

  # 5. Solve: minimise w' sigma w subject to sum(w) = 1 and w >= 0.
  n <- ncol(sigma)
  solution <- tryCatch(
    quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat = sigma, dvec = rep(0, n),
                       Amat = cbind(rep(1, n), diag(n)),
                       bvec = c(1, rep(0, n)), meq = 1L)$solution,
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(solution) || any(!is.finite(solution)) ||
      any(solution < -1e-8) || abs(sum(solution) - 1) > 1e-8) {
    return(hold("solver_failure"))
  }
  solution[solution < 0] <- 0

  # 6. Keep every holding the estimate left out, and target the rest.
  held <- ctx$universe[ctx$vec$position != 0]
  held_excluded <- if (isTRUE(keep_excluded)) setdiff(held, estimated) else character()
  target <- tryCatch(
    solution |>
      ledgr_align_weights(returns) |>
      ledgr_target_rebalance(ctx, equity_fraction = 0.95, keep = held_excluded),
    ledgr_target_sizing_unavailable = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(target)) {
    return(hold("no_permissible_mark"))
  }
  structure(target, outcome = "solved")
}
```

The parameters and their defaults:

- `lookback = 252`: the estimation window, in expected venue sessions. It is
  finite, so each decision reads the same amount of history however long the
  run is.
- `threshold = 0.2`: the largest share of carried closes an instrument may
  have in its window and still be estimated.
- `shrink = 0.5`: how far the covariance is pulled toward its diagonal, a
  fixed number in (0, 1]. Without it, a window with fewer sessions than
  instruments gives a singular covariance, and the solver fails. Half way is a
  strong pull; it keeps the estimate usable when instruments outnumber
  sessions.
- `min_obs = 60`: the fewest valid daily returns an instrument needs, about a
  quarter of the default window.
- `keep_excluded = TRUE`: keep holdings the estimate left out. It exists so
  that this article can show what happens without it.

Every returned target carries an `outcome` attribute that names how the pulse
ended. A run does not record it, but calling the strategy on one pulse shows
it.

## One Decision, Step By Step

`ledgr_pulse_snapshot()` builds the context a run would hand to the strategy
on one session. On 1 November 2019, the first session of the month, the close
read shows how much of each window was carried:

```{r}
#| label: experiment

exp <- ledgr_experiment(
  snapshot, min_variance,
  features = list(ledgr_ind_returns(1L)),
  universe = ledgr_universe_members("DEMO_UNIVERSE"),
  cost_model = ledgr_cost_zero()
)
november <- ledgr_pulse_snapshot(exp, ts_utc = as.Date("2019-11-01"), params = list())
closes <- november |> ledgr_history_frame(bar = "close", lookback = 252L)
ledgr_history_info(closes)$selection[, c("instrument_id", "requested",
                                         "carried_input_count", "carried_input_share")]
```

`DEMO_01` was delisted in January 2018, so it is not requested. `DEMO_05`'s
thin trading has carried 55 of its 252 closes, a share of 0.218, above the
threshold of 0.2: the strategy leaves it out. Return features never use a
carried close, so its return cells on those sessions are missing rather than
zero.

The return read of the remaining instruments shows how many valid daily
returns each has:

```{r}
#| label: valid-returns

selection <- ledgr_history_info(closes)$selection
candidates <- selection$instrument_id[selection$requested &
                                        selection$carried_input_share <= 0.2]
returns <- november |>
  ledgr_history_frame(feature = "return_1", lookback = 252L,
                      instruments = candidates, na_action = "keep")
colSums(is.finite(ledgr_history_matrix(returns)))
```

`DEMO_08` has traded for two months, so it has fewer than 60 valid returns and
is left out too. The five instruments that remain are estimated, and the
solver's output becomes share targets:

```{r}
#| label: one-decision
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

decision <- min_variance(november, list())
attr(decision, "outcome")
c(decision)
```

`ledgr_align_weights()` names the solver's unnamed output by the instruments
of the final return read, in the order of its columns, and refuses a vector of
the wrong length. That is why the strategy reads returns a second time after
the screen: the aligned read must hold exactly the estimated instruments.

## Decision Dates

The strategy decides on the first session of each month and returns
`ctx$hold()` on every other session. It finds the first session from a
two-session history read with no instruments: if the current session and the
previous expected session fall in the same month, this is not a decision
date. The very first session of the data has no previous session, so it
counts as a month start. Months are taken in UTC. That is right for this
venue, whose sessions close at 16:00 UTC on the venue's own civil date; for a
venue whose close falls after midnight UTC, the UTC month would differ from
the venue's month.

Before a full window of 252 sessions exists, the strategy holds as well:

```{r}
#| label: decision-dates
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

outcome_on <- function(date, params = list()) {
  ctx <- ledgr_pulse_snapshot(exp, ts_utc = as.Date(date), params = params)
  on.exit(close(ctx))
  attr(min_variance(ctx, params), "outcome")
}
outcome_on("2019-11-12")
outcome_on("2018-06-01")
```

## Run It

Preflight classifies the strategy as Tier 2, because it calls a package
outside base R. It records `quadprog` as a namespace that parallel workers
must load.

```{r}
#| label: preflight

check <- ledgr_strategy_preflight(min_variance)
check$tier
check$worker_dependencies$require_namespace
```

```{r}
#| label: run
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

bt <- exp |> ledgr_run(params = list(), run_id = "minimum-variance")
fills <- as.data.frame(ledgr_results(bt, "fills"))
fill_days <- unique(as.Date(fills$ts_utc))
length(fill_days)
head(fill_days, 4)
bt
```

The run has 36 month starts. The first twelve hold for want of a full window,
and the strategy trades after each of the other 24: the fills fall on the
session after each decision, at the next open. The summary line on corporate
actions confirms that the demo's only dividend affected no holding.

## Holdings The Estimate Leaves Out

Leaving an instrument out of the estimate is an estimation choice. It should
not sell anything by itself. But `ledgr_target_rebalance()` targets every
eligible instrument without a weight to zero, so a holding the estimate left
out would be sold at the next open. The strategy therefore passes every
holding outside the estimate in `keep`, and the rebalance keeps its quantity
and sizes the rest around it.

`DEMO_05` is held when its carried share crosses the threshold in November
2019. Its share stays above 0.2 until the thin stretch leaves the window in
July 2020:

```{r}
#| label: carried-share
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

share_on <- function(date) {
  ctx <- ledgr_pulse_snapshot(exp, ts_utc = as.Date(date), params = list())
  on.exit(close(ctx))
  selection <- ledgr_history_info(
    ctx |> ledgr_history_frame(bar = "close", lookback = 252L)
  )$selection
  selection$carried_input_share[selection$instrument_id == "DEMO_05"]
}
dates <- c("2019-10-01", "2019-11-01", "2020-06-01", "2020-07-01")
data.frame(date = dates, demo_05_share = round(vapply(dates, share_on, numeric(1)), 3))
```

Run once with `keep` and once without, and compare the `DEMO_05` fills from
October 2019 to July 2020:

```{r}
#| label: keep
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

without_keep <- exp |>
  ledgr_run(params = list(keep_excluded = FALSE), run_id = "minimum-variance-no-keep")
demo_05_fills <- function(bt) {
  fills <- as.data.frame(ledgr_results(bt, "fills"))
  fills[fills$instrument_id == "DEMO_05" &
          fills$ts_utc > as.POSIXct("2019-10-01", tz = "UTC") &
          fills$ts_utc < as.POSIXct("2020-07-31", tz = "UTC"),
        c("ts_utc", "side", "qty")]
}
demo_05_fills(bt)
demo_05_fills(without_keep)
```

With `keep`, the position is not traded while `DEMO_05` is outside the
estimate; it is rebalanced again once the estimate includes it in July 2020.
Without `keep`, the rebalance sells the whole position at the open after the
November decision and buys it back in July.

## When The Strategy Holds

On a decision date the strategy returns `ctx$hold()` instead of a target when
it cannot estimate. Each case has its own outcome:

- `not_a_decision_date` and `insufficient_history`, shown above.
- `too_few_instruments`: fewer than two instruments pass the screens. Here
  every instrument fails a `min_obs` that is longer than the window:

```{r}
#| label: too-few
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

outcome_on("2019-11-01", list(min_obs = 300L))
```

- `covariance_not_positive_definite`: the shrunk covariance has a missing
  entry or a zero or negative eigenvalue. With five sessions for seven
  instruments the sample covariance is singular, and a negligible shrinkage
  leaves it so:

```{r}
#| label: not-positive-definite
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

outcome_on("2019-11-01", list(lookback = 5L, min_obs = 2L, shrink = 1e-12))
outcome_on("2019-11-01", list(lookback = 5L, min_obs = 2L))
```

  The second call uses the default shrinkage, and the same five sessions
  give a solution.

- `solver_failure`: `solve.QP()` raises an error or returns a solution that
  does not sum to one or has a weight below zero beyond rounding. With a
  positive definite covariance and these constraints this should not happen,
  but the strategy holds rather than trade on a broken solution.
- `no_permissible_mark`: `ledgr_target_rebalance()` refuses with
  `ledgr_target_sizing_unavailable` when it must value a holding, kept or
  weighted, that has no permissible mark. The strategy catches exactly that
  class and holds.

In a run, ledgr does not let it come to that. Before the strategy is called,
every holding must have a permissible mark, a current or recent close, or a
frozen one under the default valuation policy. A run that starts from a book
holding `DEMO_08` before its first print stops at the first session:

```{r}
#| label: no-mark
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE)

book <- ledgr_experiment(
  snapshot, min_variance,
  features = list(ledgr_ind_returns(1L)),
  opening = ledgr_opening(cash = 100000, positions = c(DEMO_08 = 100),
                          cost_basis = c(DEMO_08 = 50)),
  universe = ledgr_universe_members("DEMO_UNIVERSE"),
  cost_model = ledgr_cost_zero()
)
unpriced <- book |> ledgr_run(params = list(), run_id = "minimum-variance-unpriced")
completion <- ledgr_run_completion(unpriced)
completion$completion_status
completion$stop_reason
```

The run is `INCOMPLETE` with `valuation_horizon_exhausted`: the holding could
not be valued, and the strategy was never asked to decide.

## Sweep The Window And The Threshold

The strategy reads its parameters from `params`, so the window and the
threshold are ordinary sweep parameters. Preflight told the workers to load
`quadprog`:

```{r}
#| label: sweep
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("quadprog", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)

grid <- ledgr_strategy_grid(lookback = c(126L, 252L), threshold = c(0.1, 0.2))
sweep <- ledgr_sweep(exp, grid, workers = 2L, seed = 1L)
sweep
```
